# Desktop apps: where to start

How UI, commands and document state are separated so the app stays testable and undoable, and what the files and settings it reads and writes promise across versions.

Flags: **C** contested (offer it as a choice, with both sides) · **A** agents do this readily · **T** has a one-file tell · **E** has a pseudo-code example.

Axes in brackets: ⊕ the lens's primary effect, the reason to reach for it · + also helps · − costs. Laws name the axes they bear on. See [AXES.md](../AXES.md).

`{kinds}`: where it matters most. `langs:` which languages have notes. `→` related lenses.

## Look at these first, in order

1. [`god-object`](../entries/god-object.md) **God object (The Blob)** · anti-pattern/design [AE] (delivery+ change_cost−) {mobile,games,desktop,fullstack-web,web-frontend,tui}: One class holds most of the control and data that should be spread across several, so every change goes through it. ## Probes for the interview

Find first, in the code, docs, git history, CI and config. Ask only what the repository can't tell, in the project's own terms, with the evidence and a recommendation. Skip the question when the findings settle it. Also see the general stances in [THINKING.md](../THINKING.md).

### 1. Breaking-Change Surface, Hyrum's law

**Find:** Version fields in saved files and settings, migration or upgrade code and how far back it goes, test fixtures saved by older versions, and what the docs or changelog promise about opening old files.

**Ask:** "Files carry <version field>; there are migrations from <oldest> and fixtures for <versions>. How far back do you promise to open files and settings? I'd <promise X and test it with fixtures> because <reason>."

**Settled when:** The promise is documented and fixtures cover it. The agent cites it and asks only whether it holds.

### 2. Never Change a Running System, Bus factor

**Find:** Modules with no commits in years, modules only one person has ever changed, how much other code depends on them, and comments that warn people off.

**Ask:** "<modules> haven't changed since <date>, and only <person> has ever changed <x>. Are they done, or does nobody dare? I'd <protect them with characterisation tests before any change / leave them alone> because <reason>."

**Settled when:** Never by code alone: the repo shows which parts are untouched, not why.

### 3. Production Bugs

**Find:** Fix commits sorted by layer (UI, document model, platform integration), which came with a regression test, and test counts per layer.

**Ask:** "<k> of the last <N> fixes were in <layer>, which has <few / no> tests. Did bugs reach users that don't show here? I'd require tests for <layer> because that's where fixes cluster."

**Settled when:** Never fully: the history shows fixes, not which reached users.

### 4. Ninety-ninety rule

**Find:** For features merged in the last year or so: later commits or pull requests that reference the same issue or pull request, or touch the same files within a few weeks with a fix-style message. Sort them by cause: installers and packaging, per-platform differences, undo, accessibility. Any PR checklist or definition of done.

**Ask:** "Features mostly came back for <category> (<examples>). I'd make <X> required from a feature's first commit because <reason>. Is that what holds features at almost done?"

**Settled when:** A checklist already covers what the history shows. The agent confirms it.
